# Press station -- TIA Portal starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The function block's body is yours.*

**The task.** Run the press in the mode mode.position says (0 MAN, 1 OFF, 2 AUTO), read every scan. AUTO: from Start, stroke the ram down to the bottom-dead-centre switch bdc.no, hold it there for the pot's seconds, bring it back up, and repeat until Stop or the selector leaves AUTO. OFF: the ram goes up and stays up. MAN: the ram goes down only while the two-hand relay's hands.valid is made, and comes back up when it drops or at bdc.no; the next stroke needs both hands off first.

**Done when.** In AUTO the press cycles on its own; turn the selector to OFF mid-stroke and the ram goes straight back up, and does not come down again until AUTO and Start. In MAN a click on both palms together strokes it; click one, wait a second and click the other, and hands.left and hands.right both read true while hands.valid does not -- the ram must not move, because that is what a taped-down button looks like. Take your hands off mid-stroke (a single click holds for two seconds, less than a stroke) and the ram comes back up. The mushroom (panel.estop, normally closed) stops the ram's down-stroke in any mode within 200 ms and its trip latches: releasing it restarts nothing, and neither does Start or Reset alone -- only Reset, then Start.

|---|---|

NodeIds -- is [`../README.md`](../README.md). This page is only what is
different about this scene.

## Set it up

1. In a project with an S7-1500 CPU: *External source files -> Add new
   external file*, pick `press_station.scl`, then right-click it -> *Generate
   blocks from source*. That creates `FF_IO` and `"PressStation"`. One
   exercise per CPU: this `FF_IO` replaces any other one.
2. Call `"PressStation"` from OB1 (drag it into `Main`; TIA creates the
   instance DB).
3. Check `FF_IO`'s properties: *Optimized block access* off (the source sets
   it), *Accessible from HMI/OPC UA* and *Writable from HMI/OPC UA* on for
   every member (TIA's default). Without *Writable* every sensor reads FALSE
   forever.
4. Compile, download, RUN.

## Run it

Open the scene in FactoryForge first (pick "Press station" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/press_station.json)), then attach
the sidecar with whichever driver reaches your CPU, in the folder
FactoryForge was extracted to:

```
.\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver opcua-client --mapping examples/tia/press-station/opcua_mapping.json -o url opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840
.\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver s7-snap7 -o host <cpu-ip> -o db <FF_IO's number> --mapping examples/tia/press-station/snap7_mapping.json
.\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver plcsim-advanced -o instance <name> --mapping examples/tia/press-station/plcsim_mapping.json
```

On Linux it is `./factoryforge-sidecar`. To have it marked, stop the sidecar and
start the grader in place of the 3D scene, in one terminal:

```
.\factoryforge-sidecar grade --scene press-station
```

then run the same `connect` command in a second terminal with the bus port
the grader printed added: `--port <bus port it printed>`.

<!-- from-source -->
(From a source checkout: `python -m factoryforge_sidecar` in place of
`.\factoryforge-sidecar`, with the sidecar installed and run from the repository
root so the paths resolve.)
<!-- /from-source -->

The OPC UA namespace index is usually 3, not always: run
`.\factoryforge-sidecar browse opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840` once and fix `ns=` in
the mapping if yours differs.

## FF_IO

In declaration order. `PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp);
`PLC reads` is an input (a sensor, a button, a measurement). The two
directions never share a byte, so the snap7 driver never rewrites a bit your
program owns. `FF_IO` is 12 bytes. *Brief* marks the signals the task
names.

| Tag | Direction | Member | Type | Offset | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | `PanelGreen` | Bool | DBX0.0 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | `PanelRed` | Bool | DBX0.1 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `ram.extend` | PLC writes | `RamExtend` | Bool | DBX0.2 | extend coil (5/2 valve, no spring: the rod stays where it was last driven) | yes |
| `ram.retract` | PLC writes | `RamRetract` | Bool | DBX0.3 | retract coil | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | `TowerGreen` | Bool | DBX0.4 | tower lamp, green | yes |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | `TowerRed` | Bool | DBX0.5 | tower lamp, red | yes |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | `TowerYellow` | Bool | DBX0.6 | tower lamp, yellow | yes |
| `mode.position` | PLC reads | `ModePosition` | DInt | DBD2 | selector position, 0-based, in the order MAN,OFF,AUTO; it stays where it is put | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | `PanelSetpoint` | Real | DBD6 | the operator's pot, 0.5..5 s (starts at 1) | yes |
| `bdc.nc` | PLC reads | `BdcNc` | Bool | DBX10.0 | limit switch NC contact: TRUE at rest, FALSE while the lever is pushed | yes |
| `bdc.no` | PLC reads | `BdcNo` | Bool | DBX10.1 | limit switch NO contact: TRUE while the lever is pushed past its trip point | yes |
| `hands.left` | PLC reads | `HandsLeft` | Bool | DBX10.2 | left palm button held | yes |
| `hands.right` | PLC reads | `HandsRight` | Bool | DBX10.3 | right palm button held | yes |
| `hands.valid` | PLC reads | `HandsValid` | Bool | DBX10.4 | the two-hand relay's permissive: both held AND pressed within 0.5 s -- not left AND right | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | `PanelEstop` | Bool | DBX10.5 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | `PanelReset` | Bool | DBX10.6 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | `PanelStart` | Bool | DBX10.7 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | `PanelStop` | Bool | DBX11.0 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `ram.extended` | PLC reads | `RamExtended` | Bool | DBX11.1 | reed switch at full stroke | yes |
| `ram.fault` | PLC reads | `RamFault` | Bool | DBX11.2 | TRUE = the cylinder has seized |  |
| `ram.retracted` | PLC reads | `RamRetracted` | Bool | DBX11.3 | reed switch at home; mid-stroke neither reed is made | yes |

`int` travels as a `DInt` and `float` as a `Real`: the OPC UA driver writes
Int32 and Float, and a member of any other type is refused as a type mismatch.
Hold anything the scene must see for well over a second on OPC UA: an
S7-1500 forces a 1000 ms publishing interval on subscriptions, which is why the
driver polls by default.
